note: Adjective governance for Kumulus sell-side writing (Plan §15), with usage counts observed in the 753 real Bones+Torino bullets. Class A = safe with basic factual support; Class B = requires stronger evidence; Class C = use rarely, needs clear justification. Counts show what the house actually leans on — 'strong' (31) and 'recurring' (28) are overused; vary them.

classA_safe.rule: Usable with basic factual support in the deal.

classB_needs_evidence.rule: Only with specific supporting evidence (ranking, margin data, retention, tenure, etc). See claim->evidence table in the guide.

classC_rare.rule: Avoid unless externally substantiated; the house barely uses these (good discipline — keep it).

claimEvidence.leading: ranking, market share, scale, recognized position
claimEvidence.experienced: tenure, years in sector, track record
claimEvidence.loyal: retention, tenure, repeat sales, low churn
claimEvidence.diversified: revenue split by customer / product / geography / sector
claimEvidence.high-margin: reported margin data or relative product economics
claimEvidence.recurring: contract structure, consumables usage, installed base, repeat purchase
claimEvidence.resilient: historical stability, defensive end-markets, recurring demand
claimEvidence.scalable: capacity, systems, operating leverage, expansion model
